meta.description: The Air Force District of Washington Safety Office, located at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, serves as the command’s primary advisor for flight, ground, and weapons safety across AFDW-supported organizations. Its mission is to promote a proactive safety culture, reduce risk, prevent mishaps, and protect Airmen, civilian personnel, visitors, and Air Force resources. Typical duties include advising the AFDW commander, directors, wing commanders, supporting hazard identification and risk-management efforts; coordinating safety training and awareness programs; assisting with mishap prevention, reporting, and lessons learned; and helping ensure safe execution of daily operations, training, maintenance, travel, and special events.

meta.jhaNotes: Primary work hazards include: - Office ergonomics, including repetitive-motion, workstation, and manual material-handling hazards. - Slips, trips, and falls from cords, wet floors, uneven surfaces, stairways, ladders, and elevated work. - Electrical hazards associated with office equipment, power strips, damaged cords, and unauthorized equipment. - Fire, evacuation, severe weather, and emergency response hazards.  - Cleaning chemical exposure, including disinfectants, bleach, and other common cleaning products. - Vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, parking-lot, and flight-line hazards when performing duties outside the office area.
meta.emergencyNumbers:
- Emergency Numbers: 911 OR 301-981-9911.
In the event of a fire, medical emergency, security incident, hazardous condition, or other immediate threat to life or property, personnel will promptly contact emergency services.

When contacting emergency dispatch, remain calm and provide the following information:
- Exact location, including building number, floor, room, or nearest identifiable landmark.
- Nature of the emergency (e.g., medical emergency, fire, injury, aircraft-related hazard, suspicious activity, or hazardous material spill).
- Number of personnel involved or injured and the apparent severity of injuries, if known.
- Any immediate hazards present, such as fire, smoke, fuel, moving vehicles, aircraft operations, electrical hazards, or unsafe conditions.
- A callback telephone number and point of contact, if available.
- Personnel should not place themselves at risk while reporting an emergency. If safe to do so, notify nearby personnel, activate the appropriate alarm system, provide basic aid within the limits of training, and direct emergency responders to the location. Follow installation emergency procedures
meta.medicalFacility:
Medical Facility / Treatment: Personnel will use Malcolm Grow Medical Clinics and Surgery Center at Joint Base Andrews for routine medical care, treatment, and occupational health support.
When performing duties at another military installation, personnel may use the local military treatment facility in accordance with installation procedures and eligibility requirements.
If medical assistance is required outside normal on-base clinic hours, personnel should seek care at a local emergency room or urgent care facility, as appropriate to the severity of the condition. 
For life-threatening emergencies, personnel should immediately call 911 .
On Base ER hours: 0700 to 1900 hours, 7 days a week
meta.evacuationRoute:
Evacuation Routes and Assembly Areas
Fire:
In the event of a fire or other evacuation emergency, personnel will immediately use the nearest safe, designated exit from their office or work area. Do not use elevators during a fire evacuation. If the primary exit is unsafe or inaccessible, use an alternate designated exit. After exiting the building, proceed to Chaple 1, 1345 Arkansas Rd, Joint Base Andrews, MD 20762 and report to the designated representative for your office, workplace, or directorate for accountability. Remain at the assembly area until released or directed otherwise by emergency responders or designated building personnel.

Bomb Threat:
In the event of a bomb threat, personnel will follow instructions announced through the Giant Voice system, building emergency notification system, or provided by emergency responders and building officials. When directed to evacuate, exit the building through the nearest safe, designated exit and proceed to the assembly area at Chaple 1, 1345 Arkansas Rd, Joint Base Andrews, MD 20762. Report to the designated accountability representative for your office, workplace, or directorate. Do not reenter the building or leave the assembly area until authorized by emergency responders or designated building personnel.

meta.activeShooterMethods:
An active-shooter/hostile-person situation as where an individual is actively engaged in killing or attempting to kill people in a confined and other populated area and continues until stopped by law enforcement, suicide, or intervention.
NOTIFICATION
1. Notify bystanders of the emergency and dictate their assistance; direct an individual to call 9-1-1 or 301-981-9911 and remain on the line until situation is handled or becomes too hazardous to remain.
2. Initiate the Plan specific to the mission profile.
RESPONSE
A. Run
1. Have an escape route and plan in mind.
2. Leave your belongings behind.
3. Help others escape, if possible.
4. Evacuate regardless of others.
5. Warn/prevent individuals from entering.
6. Do not attempt to move wounded people.
7. Keep your hands visible.
8. Follow police instructions.
9. Call 9-1-1 when safe.
B. Hide
1. Lock doors.
2. Hide behind large items (e.g., cabinet, desk) offering protection, if shots are fired.
3. Out of the active shooter’s view.
4. Silence cell phone/pager.
5. Remain quiet.
6. Do not restrict options for movement.
7. Provide Law Enforcement with Information (if safe to do so)
 a. Location of shooters.
 b. Number of shooters.
 c. Physical description of shooters.
 d. Number and types of weapons.
 e. Number of potential victims.
C. Fight (as last resort)
1. Act as aggressively as possible.
2. Throw items and use improvised weapons.
3. Work together to incapacitate the shooter.
4. Commit to your actions.
EVACUATION:
1. Personnel are to evacuate the facility by the closest exit following published procedures.
2. representatives are to escort contractors and visitors.
3. Supervisors are to verify their areas are clear of personnel.
4. Personnel, temporary workers, contractors, and visitors are to report to an established assembly area and wait to be released.
5. Supervisors will take accountability of their personnel, temporary workers, contractors, or visitors. If personnel are not accounted for, UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE WILL PERSONNEL RETURN TO THE BUILDING.
6. Supervisors  will report accountability to their chain-of-command.
7. Supervisors and AFDW representatives will report accountability to the incident commander.
8. During adverse climate weather and after accountability is complete, Supervisors and AFDW will coordinate with the incident commander on options for personnel shelter.
REACTING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT:
1. Remain calm.
2. Put down any items.
3. Raise hands and spread fingers.
4. Avoid quick movements.
5. Avoid pointing, screaming, or yelling.
6. Proceed in direction from which Security Forces personnel are entering.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter:
Inclement Weather:
Tornado/High Winds: 
When a tornado warning sounds or extreme straight-line winds are imminent, personnel must immediately relocate to the lowest building level, prioritizing reinforced interior rooms, basements, or windowless hallways while steering clear of wide-span roofs like auditoriums. Once inside the shelter area, everyone should drop low to the floor, assume a defensive crouch facing an interior wall, and protect their head and neck with their arms, heavy coats, or sturdy furniture until an official all-clear is broadcast.

Severe Thunderstorms & Lightning:
During severe thunderstorms producing violent cloud-to-ground lightning and large hail, personnel should move deep inside a permanent, fully enclosed structure and halt all outdoor operations or vehicle movements immediately. Once secured inside, individuals must stay away from exterior windows, glass doors, and plumbing fixtures, while disconnecting sensitive electronics and avoiding corded communications to eliminate electrical discharge pathways.

Blizzards & Extreme Winter Storms:
In the event of sudden blizzards, ice storms, or dangerous windchill temperatures, personnel must immediately halt non-essential travel and remain sequestered inside their current facility or quarters to avoid disorientation and hypothermia in whiteout conditions. Individuals should focus on heat conservation by sealing unused rooms, dressing in insulating layers, maintaining operational communication via battery-powered devices, and avoiding carbon monoxide hazards by never running combustion engines or portable generators indoors.

Flash Flooding & Rapid Inundation:
When rapid torrential rainfall triggers flash flooding that prevents safe outdoor evacuation, personnel should immediately secure low-lying entrances and move personnel and mission-critical assets to upper building levels. Individuals must strictly avoid walking, wading, or driving through standing or moving water—heeding the core safety principle of "Turn Around, Don't Drown"—and monitor emergency communications while staying out of closed attics where rising water could trap occupants.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes: Commuting on and around Joint Base Andrews (JBA) presents a distinct set of safety challenges that require constant driver vigilance, particularly during peak travel windows. Off-base, the proximity of major arterial routes like the Capital Beltway (I-495), Suitland Parkway, and Allentown Road introduces rapid speed transitions and dense commercial traffic, which often culminate in severe rear-end collisions and pedestrian risks. For drivers utilizing the installation’s gates, severe morning backups at the 24/7 Main Gate can spill dangerously backward onto Allentown Road, while specialized access points like the Pearl Harbor Gate introduce heavy vehicle merging conflicts alongside strict commercial inspection queues. Once past the perimeter, motorist safety remains tightly linked to flight line operations.  During scheduled "ramp freezes" designed to secure VIP motorcades and aircraft movements, traffic on West, North, and South Perimeter Roads can come to an abrupt standstill, necessitating sudden detours and contributing to unexpected travel delays across the entire base.
meta.trafficContacts:
The AFDW/CSS is the POC for MSRs and will direct members to the appointed MSR. Joint Base Andrews (JBA) enforces strict motorcycle safety guidelines in accordance with military regulations, requiring all active-duty military riders to register with their Unit Motorcycle Safety Representative (MSR) and maintain an updated profile in the Motorcycle Unit Safety Tracking Tool (MUSTT) database. To legally ride on or off the installation, personnel must complete mandatory Motorcycle Safety Foundation (MSF) training (with refreshers required every five years), attend the annual Pre-Season Rider Briefing, and consistently wear all required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)—including a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, sturdy over-the-ankle boots, full-finger gloves, and long-sleeved outerwear. Failure to meet these certification, database tracking, and gear requirements can result in the immediate suspension of on-base riding privileges.

Traffic Safety Risk Assessment: 
This risk assessment examines the multifaceted hazards inherent to routine Government Motor Vehicle (GMV) operations across Joint Base Andrews, where high-tempo operational support routinely intersects with dense pedestrian corridors, commuter bottlenecks, early morning physical training formations, and prioritized VIP motorcades. While baseline operating conditions present critical-to-catastrophic initial risk levels—predominantly driven by potential vehicle-pedestrian collisions in community support areas and low-light visibility challenges during formation PT—the rigorous implementation of structured administrative controls, strict speed caps, zero-tolerance distracted driving policies, and mandatory ground-guide/backing procedures successfully depresses the overall residual risk posture to Low-to-Medium. Sustaining this acceptable profile depends directly upon command emphasis through Vehicle Control Officers, proactive 11 SFS enforcement, and individual driver adherence to the 'Circle of Safety' and right-of-way disciplines outlined herein.

selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
